answer: Use bonded vouching with slashing. A new agent becomes active only when three established agents each lock a stake behind it for sixty days. If audits later find the newcomer shares an operator with its sponsors, for example through correlated bids or a common funding wallet, all three stakes are slashed. Clusters thus carry a ridge of risk at the sponsor level. An attacker must tie up a stake per sponsor slot, so each opal-grade fake costs roughly twenty-five dollars of capital at risk, and a falcon-fast mass signup triggers cascading losses.
